questions.statement: Choose the correct article: 'She is ____ engineer with a well-known company.'
questions.context: Practica de articulos, San Salvador.

options.feedback: Countable singular professions take the indefinite article 'a'.
'An' is used before vowels, and 'engineer' begins with a consonant sound.
'The' would imply a specific engineer already mentioned.
A countable singular noun needs a determiner before it.

questions.explanation:
Las profesiones se introducen con el articulo indefinido 'a' cuando se habla de una profession en general.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence uses 'the' correctly?
questions.context: Uso del articulo definido, San Miguel.

options.text: A sun rises in the east.
options.feedback: The sun is unique, so 'a sun' incorrectly suggests one of many.
A count noun needs an article even in a general statement.

options.text: The a sun rises in the east.
options.feedback: Two articles cannot be combined.

options.text: The sun rises in the east.
options.feedback: 'The sun' is a unique object known to everyone, so the definite article is required.

questions.explanation:
'The' se usa cuando hay algo unico y conocido: 'the sun' es un referente unico para todos los hablantes.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'I would like ____ egg and some bread, please.'
questions.context: Articulos con sustantivos contables e incontables, San Salvador.

options.feedback: 'A' is used before consonants; 'egg' begins with a vowel sound.
'An egg' is the correct countable singular form, contrasting with 'some bread'.
'Some' is correct with the uncountable 'bread' but not with a countable singular noun.
'Many' is used with plural count nouns only.

questions.explanation:
'Egg' es contable singular y empieza por vocal, por lo que lleva 'an'; 'bread' es incontable y ya lleva 'some'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Look at the sentence: 'He is ____ best student in the class.' Choose the correct article.
questions.context: Superlativos y articulos, San Miguel.

options.feedback: Superlative adjectives are preceded by 'the'.
'A' cannot introduce a superlative comparison.
'An' cannot introduce a superlative comparison.
The definite article is mandatory before a superlative.

questions.explanation:
Los superlativos exigen el articulo definido: la forma correcta es 'the best student'.

questions.statement: Which sentence is correct?
questions.context: Evaluacion del uso de articulos, San Salvador.

options.text: She works as nurse at the hospital.
options.feedback: A countable singular profession requires the article 'a'.

options.text: She works as the nurse at the hospital.
options.feedback: 'The' would imply a nurse already mentioned or unique in the context.

options.text: She works as a nurse at the hospital.
options.feedback: 'As a nurse' follows the standard pattern 'as' plus indefinite article plus profession.

options.text: She works as an nurse at the hospital.
options.feedback: 'An' is used before a vowel sound; 'nurse' begins with the consonant sound /n/.

questions.explanation:
El patron estandar para nombrar una profession es 'as' mas articulo indefinido mas sustantivo.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct article: 'He is ____ honest boy.'
questions.context: Articulos con adjectives que empiezan por vocal, San Salvador.

options.feedback: The spelling begins with a consonant letter, but the rule follows the sound, not the letter.
The initial 'h' in 'honest' is silent, so the vowel sound requires 'an'.
'The' would imply a specific boy already mentioned.
A countable singular noun requires a determiner.

questions.explanation:
Aunque 'honest' empieza por 'h', la 'h' es muda, de modo que el sonido inicial es vocal y corresponde 'an'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete: 'Water is ____ of the most important natural resources.'
questions.context: Sustantivos incontables y superlativos, San Salvador.

options.feedback: 'A of the' is not a valid construction in English.
'An of the' is grammatically impossible.
'Many' is used with plural count nouns, not before 'of the'.
'One of the most important' is the correct superlative construction.

questions.explanation:
En una comparacion superlativa el articulo aparece antes de 'of': 'the most important of the most important' no, sino 'one of the most important'.

questions.statement: Choose the correct question: '____ is the capital of El Salvador?'
questions.context: Interrogacion con articulo definido, San Salvador.

options.feedback: 'What is the capital...?' is the standard neutral question.
'Which' selects among several known options, which is not the case here.
'Whose' asks about possession, not about identification.
'Where' asks about a place, not about the name of a city.

questions.explanation:
La pregunta por un objeto unico y conocido requiere el articulo definido 'the'. 'The' aparece tambien en 'the capital of El Salvador'.

questions.statement: Look at this sentence and choose the best correction: 'I am student at the university.'
questions.context: Correccion de errores con articulos, San Salvador.

options.feedback: 'The' would imply a specific student already known to the listener.
That would change the meaning; the original states a generic role.
The singular form is intended; only the article is missing.
A countable singular noun needs a determiner: 'I am a student'.

questions.explanation:
A un sustantivo contable singular le falta el articulo: la forma correcta es 'I am a student'.

questions.statement: Which sentence uses the articles correctly?
questions.context: Consolidacion de articulos, San Miguel.

options.text: He drank glass of milk and the water in it.
options.feedback: A countable singular noun cannot appear without a determiner.

options.text: He drank a glass of milk and a water in it.
options.feedback: 'A water' is not acceptable for the specific liquid already mentioned.

options.text: He drank a glass of milk and the water in it.
options.feedback: 'A glass' is countable and 'the water' is the specific water referred to.

options.text: He drank a glass of the milk and water in it.
options.feedback: 'The milk' would imply milk previously identified; this is its first mention.

questions.explanation:
Cada sustantivo recibe el articulo que le corresponde segun si es contable y si el referente ya esta identificado.

questions.statement: Complete: 'My uncle is ____ pilot and my aunt is ____ engineer.'
questions.context: Articulos con professions, San Salvador.

options.feedback: 'A pilot' before a consonant sound and 'an engineer' before a vowel sound.
The article order is reversed: consonant takes 'a', vowel takes 'an'.
'An' is required before a vowel sound such as the initial /e/ of 'engineer'.
'A' is required before a consonant sound such as /p/ in 'pilot'.

questions.explanation:
'Pilot' empieza con sonido consonante y lleva 'a'; 'engineer' empieza con vocal y lleva 'an'.

questions.statement: Which noun is normally used without an article?
questions.context: Sustantivos incontables en plural, San Salvador.

options.feedback: 'Chair' is a countable noun and normally takes 'a' or 'the'.
'Furniture' is uncountable: no plural form, no article, verb in the singular.
'Table' is countable and requires an article.
'Lamp' is countable and requires an article.

questions.explanation:
Los sustantivos incontables como 'furniture', 'information' o 'advice' no tienen forma plural y no llevan articulo.

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'I need ____ information about the trip.'
questions.context: Sustantivos incontables en contexto academico, San Miguel.

options.feedback: Uncountable nouns never take the indefinite article 'a'.
'Some information' is the correct treatment for an uncountable singular noun.
Uncountable nouns never take 'an'.
'Many' requires a plural count noun; 'information' has no plural.

questions.explanation:
'Information' es incontable, de modo que no lleva 'a' ni 'an'; en este contexto conviene 'some'.

questions.statement: Choose the sentence where the article is used correctly.
questions.context: Analisis de articulos en contexto especifico, San Salvador.

options.text: I saw a dog. The dog was very big.
options.feedback: The first mention is indefinite; the second uses 'the' because the dog is now identified.

options.text: I saw a dog. A dog was very big.
options.feedback: The second 'a' suggests a different, unspecified dog.

options.text: I saw the dog. The dog was very big.
options.feedback: The first mention should be indefinite for a dog the listener does not know.

options.text: I saw a dog. This dog was very big.
options.feedback: 'This' requires a listener already focused on the animal.

questions.explanation:
El articulo indefinido se usa ante algo no identificado por primera vez; 'the' senala algo ya identificable.

questions.statement: What does 'the' do in the phrase 'the United Nations'?
questions.context: Nombres propios de organizaciones, San Salvador.

options.text: It indicates a plural collective noun.
options.feedback: The article does not change the number of the name.
'The' is a determiner, not a preposition.

options.text: It identifies the organisation as a single unique entity.
options.feedback: 'The' marks a unique institution built into the proper name.
Possession is expressed with an apostrophe-s or with 'of', not with 'the'.

questions.explanation:
En nombres de organizaciones se usa 'the' cuando el nombre incluye un especificador como 'United' o 'Republic'.

questions.statement: Choose the best completion: 'The children are playing ____ park near the school.'
questions.context: Preposiciones y articulos en un mismo contexto, San Salvador.

options.feedback: 'A park' would introduce any park, not the one near the school.
'An' cannot be used before the consonant sound of 'park'.
A countable singular noun needs a determiner.
'The park' refers to a specific park already known in the context.

questions.explanation:
Aqui se trata de un lugar especifico y ya mencionado, por lo que se usa el articulo definido 'the'.

questions.statement: Which statement about the zero article is correct?
questions.context: Usos del articulo cero, San Miguel.

options.text: It is used before all countable singular nouns.
options.feedback: Countable singular nouns normally require 'a' or 'the'.

options.text: It is used after every preposition.
options.feedback: Articles appear in many prepositional phrases, as in 'in the park'.

options.text: It is used before languages, subjects and meals in general.
options.feedback: The zero article covers generalisations like 'Spanish', 'mathematics' and 'breakfast'.

options.text: It is never used with uncountable nouns.
options.feedback: Uncountable generalisations, like 'water is important', use the zero article.

questions.explanation:
El articulo cero aparece ante nombres de disciplinas, lenguas, comidas en general, dias y meses.

questions.statement: Choose the sentence in which every article is correct.
questions.context: Evaluacion integral de articulos, San Miguel.

options.text: He is doctor and lives in city near the mountain.
options.feedback: The countable nouns 'doctor' and 'city' lack their required articles.

options.text: He is a doctor and lives in the city near the mountain.
options.feedback: 'A doctor' (first mention) and the specific places all take the correct articles.

options.text: He is a doctor and lives in a city near a mountain.
options.feedback: The second mention of specific places requires 'the', not 'a'.

options.text: He is the doctor and lives in a city near mountain.
options.feedback: The first mention of the profession and the mountain needs the correct articles.

questions.explanation:
En esta oracion, 'a' acompana a una profession y 'the' identifica los lugares especificos ya mencionados.

questions.statement: Complete: '____ Spanish is spoken in many countries, but ____ Spanish of El Salvador has particular words.'
questions.context: Articulos con lenguas y variedades, San Salvador.

options.feedback: The article assignment is inverted with respect to standard usage.
'A Spanish' would treat the language as a countable item, which is not correct.
'Spanish' in general takes the zero article; 'the Spanish of El Salvador' is a specific variety.
The second use specifies a variety and therefore requires 'the'.

options.feedback: Both articles are missing; 'manager' is a countable singular noun.

options.text: Is the manager in office now?
options.feedback: 'In the office' needs the article after the preposition.

options.text: Is a manager in the office now?
options.feedback: 'A manager' would refer to a different person from the known manager.

La pregunta conserva el articulo que corresponde: 'the manager' lleva 'the' tanto en la pregunta como en la afirmacion.
